extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114 including eligibility, required elements, timing relative to allowance/appeal/Board/court actions, and examiner notice/form usage. Focused on examiner procedures and applicant consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that complies with 35 U.S.C. 371. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requirement recurs for RCEs filed after allowance, after appeal, after a Board decision, etc. Form paragraph usage and examiner notices should only be used if the application meets these eligibility prerequisites. If application is not of the eligible type, use the Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051) prepared by technical support personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of a proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper RCE must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and include a submission as required by 37 CFR 1.114. The submission may include an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an RCE to be 'proper' the submission should be responsive (within meaning of 37 CFR 1.111) to the last outstanding Office action. If the submission is not fully responsive but is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, the applicant should be notified of deficiencies and given a new time period to complete the reply (use form paragraph 7.42.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when RCE is filed after payment of the issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after the issue fee has been paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue must have been filed and granted for prosecution to be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition was filed and granted, prosecution will be reopened but applicant may not obtain a refund of the issue fee. If the application is subsequently allowed, the Notice of Allowance will reflect an issue fee amount equal to the difference between the current issue fee and the issue fee previously paid. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an RCE after Notice of Appeal but before a Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after filing a Notice of Appeal to the PTAB but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper (see 37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE. Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in an application containing an appeal awaiting decision; otherwise, the Board may refuse to vacate a decision rendered after filing of an RCE. Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.06) to notify applicant that the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper RCE after appeal — entry and consideration of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE is accompanied by the fee (37 CFR 1.17(e)) and a submission that includes a reply responsive under 37 CFR 1.111 to the last outstanding Office action, the Office will withdraw the finality of the last Office action and the submission will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is not fully responsive but is a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, notify applicant that the submission is not fully responsive and give a new time period to complete the reply (use form paragraph 7.42.08). Use form paragraph 7.42.06 when the RCE is proper to notify that appeal withdrawn and prosecution reopened. See 37 CFR 1.135(c) and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after appeal — characterization and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed after appeal that lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e), or the submission required by 37 CFR 1.114, or both, is an improper RCE. The appeal will nevertheless be withdrawn pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is improper and there are no allowed claims, the application is abandoned. If there is at least one allowed claim, pass the application to issue on the allowed claim(s). If allowed claims exist but formal matters are outstanding, give a shortened statutory period of two months to correct formal matters (see form paragraphs 7.42.10–7.42.14). Claims allowable only by virtue of dependency on rejected claims are to be treated as rejected and canceled. See MPEP § 1215.01 for detailed handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after a Board decision but before further appeal or civil action — timeliness and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed after a PTAB decision but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action will withdraw finality and reopen prosecution if timely filed; generally the deadline to file a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit is sixty-three (63) days after the final Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filed within the 63-day period and before filing of a notice of appeal is timely. Note the res judicata effect of a Board decision: a Board decision is the 'law of the case' and is controlling in that application and related applications. A submission containing arguments without amendment of rejected claims or a showing of facts will not be effective to remove new grounds of rejection entered by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision — handling of submissions and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but lacks the required fee and/or submission, the RCE is improper and any time period running was not tolled by the improper request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.16 to notify applicant that the RCE is improper. If time for seeking court review has passed, include the form paragraph with a Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment as appropriate; if time still remains, use it on a PTOL-90 with no time period set. Generally do not enter a submission filed with an improper RCE; exception: an amendment that obviously places the application in condition for allowance may be entered with supervisory approval (see MPEP § 1214.07). If the application is not the eligible type, use PTO-2051 (Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE availability relative to Federal Circuit appeal or civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure under 37 CFR 1.114 is not available in an application after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action in federal district court, unless the appeal or civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed in an application that has undergone court review, the examiner should bring the application to a supervisory patent examiner or quality assurance specialist to determine propriety. Unless the application contains allowed claims (or the court's mandate indicates further action), the termination of an unsuccessful appeal or civil action results in abandonment of the application. See MPEP § 1216.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and form paragraphs to be used for RCE notices and transmittals
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/30, 'Request for Continued Examination (RCE) Transmittal,' may be used by applicant. The Office uses form paragraphs 7.42.05–7.42.16 for various notices regarding RCEs; the Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE), Form PTO-2051, is used by technical support personnel to notify applicant that continued examination does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form paragraphs according to the factual situation (e.g., 7.42.05 for RCE after payment of issue fee with petition granted; 7.42.06 after appeal but before Board decision where RCE is proper; 7.42.07 after Board decision; 7.42.10–7.42.14 for specific situations when appeal withdrawn and claims allowed/abandoned; 7.42.16 for improper RCE after Board decision). Use PTOL-90 where appropriate to preserve time for court review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period and extensions for correcting formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When an improper RCE results in passing to issue but formal matters remain, applicant should be given a shortened statutory period of two months to correct the formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136, but no extension can carry the date for reply beyond the maximum period of six months set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133). Use the two-month shortened period language when mailing notices in these circumstances (see form paragraphs 7.42.12 and 7.42.14).
